claude.sample_unit: elective outpatients undergoing invasive coronary angiography

links.outcome: Local model AUROC on geographical validation vs local test set, then after refitting on provincial data
links.effect: Local model AUROC fell from 0.807 to 0.714 on rest of province; after updating on provincial data AUROC recovered to 0.794.
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the geographical validation cohort than on the local test set (AUROC = 0.714 [95% CI: 0.714, 0.714] vs. 0.807 [95% CI: 0.806, 0.808]).

links.outcome: Model AUROC and impact reported separately by site across 20 hospital corporations
links.effect: Local model AUROC across sites ranged from 0.851 to 0.608; after updating, sites ranged from 0.872 to 0.720.
links.quote: AUROC across individual sites ranged from a high of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.850, 0.852) to a low of 0.608 (95% CI: 0.607, 0.609).

links.outcome: Discrimination before and after refitting model on representative provincial data with site-level calibration and thresholds
links.effect: Provincial refit AUROC 0.794 vs 0.714 for local model on other sites; ICAs avoided 27 of 39 vs 21 of 36; performance recovered across all sites.
links.quote: Following updating, model AUROC recovered almost entirely at 0.794 (95% CI: 0.794, 0.795) compared with 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808) for the original local test set.

links.outcome: Temporal drift in AUROC using sliding-window annual updating simulation
links.effect: AUROC dropped to 0.724 and 0.737 in 2020-21 and 0.670 and 0.677 in 2022-23 versus 0.807 on local test set; updating on the full data recovered performance.
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the temporal validation cohort than on the local test set, with a moderate drop in AUROC in 2020 (0.724 [95% CI: 0.722, 0.727]) and 2021 (0.737 [95% CI: 0.735, 0.739]), followed by a larger drop for 2022 (0.670 [95% CI: 0.668, 0.673]) and 2023 (0.677 [95% CI: 0.672, 0.681]).

links.outcome: Model performance and impact across sex, age, ethnicity and marginalization subgroups
links.effect: Local model AUROC lowest for Black patients (0.612); after provincial updating ethnic differences narrowed (0.749-0.790). Benefit skewed to females (42/50 ICAs avoided vs 18/32 for males).
links.quote: The local model performed best for Asian patients (AUROC = 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705]) and worst for Black patients (AUROC = 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614]).

links.outcome: Fairness metrics across demographic subgroups and sites beyond aggregate results
links.effect: Aggregate AUROC hid subgroup and site gaps: local model AUROC 0.608-0.851 across sites; ICA avoided 13/29 for men vs 34/47 for women; updating narrowed ethnic gaps.
links.quote: There is some variation in the performance of the local model for patients of different ethnicities in the external validation cohort.

links.outcome: Performance of model when applied to new regions and time periods
links.effect: Performance predictably decreased in new regions and periods (AUROC 0.714 geographic; 0.670-0.737 temporal) versus 0.807 locally.
links.quote: Our study showed that while model performance predictably decreases when applied to new regions (rural vs. urban, academic vs. community hospital) or time periods (pre-pandemic, COVID 19 pandemic, and post-pandemic), performance recovers following model updating.

links.outcome: Differences between development and validation cohort populations and their effect on performance
links.effect: Cohorts differed significantly on most predictors (e.g. racialized/newcomer ON-Marg -0.384 vs 0.196, translator required 1.05% vs 9.2%); performance dropped on geographical validation.
links.quote: Notably, while the distribution of patients by sex was stable both geographically and temporally, patients in the temporal validation cohort were nearly 2 years older on average than those in the model derivation cohort.

links.outcome: Distribution of benefit (unnecessary ICAs avoided) across sex, age and ethnic groups
links.effect: Provincial model benefits skewed toward females (42/50 avoided vs 18/32 males) and under-65 (33/43 vs 20/34), though these groups had higher baseline unnecessary ICA rates.
links.quote: Benefits, however, were skewed heavily towards females, with 42 out of every 50 unnecessary ICAs avoided (specificity: 83.3%) compared with only 18 out of every 32 (specificity: 56.5%) for males (see Supplementary material online , Figure S4 ).

links.outcome: Whether historical label bias affected equity; prospective equity assessment
links.effect: Model trained on objective angiographic labels; groups with higher baseline unnecessary ICA (women, Black, under 65) saw larger reductions, though ethnicity was missing for 57%.
links.quote: However, since our model was trained using an objective measure of disease for labelling rather than a proxy measure, our model appears to have overcome the historical bias built into the training set.

unlisted_practices: Site-specific decision threshold optimization using Youden's index to account for regional event-rate variation
Sliding-window annual model refitting to simulate scheduled updating

links.outcome: geographic external validation performance
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the geographical validation cohort than on the local test set (AUROC = 0.714 [95% CI: 0.714, 0.714] vs. 0.807 [95% CI: 0.806, 0.808]).

links.outcome: performance variation across sites
links.quote: AUROC across individual sites ranged from a high of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.850, 0.852) to a low of 0.608 (95% CI: 0.607, 0.609).

links.outcome: temporal validation performance
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the temporal validation cohort than on the local test set, with a moderate drop in AUROC in 2020 (0.724 [95% CI: 0.722, 0.727]) and 2021 (0.737 [95% CI: 0.735, 0.739]), followed by a larger drop for 2022 (0.670 [95% CI: 0.668, 0.673]) and 2023 (0.677 [95% CI: 0.672, 0.681]).

links.outcome: ethnicity subgroup AUROC
links.effect: Local model AUROC was 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705] for Asian patients and 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614] for Black patients.
links.quote: The local model performed best for Asian patients (AUROC = 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705]) and worst for Black patients (AUROC = 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614]).

links.outcome: provincial model updating performance
links.effect: After updating, AUROC recovered to 0.794 (95% CI: 0.794, 0.795) vs 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808).
links.quote: Following updating, model AUROC recovered almost entirely at 0.794 (95% CI: 0.794, 0.795) compared with 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808) for the original local test set.

links.outcome: ethnicity missingness for fairness
links.effect: Ethnicity was unknown for 57% of patients, limiting fairness analysis.
links.quote: Finally, fairness analysis for ethnicity is limited by a high rate of missingness—many Canadian healthcare organizations have historically not collected data on patients’ ethnicity; thus, ethnicity is unknown for 57% of patients in our cohort—so these results should be interpreted with caution.

links.outcome: estimated reduction in unnecessary ICAs
links.effect: 27 of every 39 unnecessary ICAs could be avoided through model use.
links.quote: Analysis of health system impact indicates that 27 of every 39 unnecessary ICAs could be avoided through use of the model.

links.outcome: discrimination performance on external geographical cohort versus local test set
links.effect: AUROC was significantly lower in the geographical validation cohort at 0.714 (95% CI: 0.714, 0.714) compared with 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808) in the local test set.
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the geographical validation cohort than on the local test set (AUROC = 0.714 [95% CI: 0.714, 0.714] vs. 0.807 [95% CI: 0.806, 0.808]).

links.outcome: discrimination performance across individual cardiac catheterization sites
links.effect: AUROC across individual sites ranged from 0.608 (95% CI: 0.607, 0.609) to 0.851 (95% CI: 0.850, 0.852).
links.quote: AUROC across individual sites ranged from a high of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.850, 0.852) to a low of 0.608 (95% CI: 0.607, 0.609).

links.outcome: discrimination performance of local model across consecutive temporal validation years
links.effect: AUROC dropped from 0.807 on the local test set to 0.724 in 2020, 0.737 in 2021, 0.670 in 2022, and 0.677 in 2023.
links.quote: As expected, performance of the local model was lower on the temporal validation cohort than on the local test set, with a moderate drop in AUROC in 2020 (0.724 [95% CI: 0.722, 0.727]) and 2021 (0.737 [95% CI: 0.735, 0.739]), followed by a larger drop for 2022 (0.670 [95% CI: 0.668, 0.673]) and 2023 (0.677 [95% CI: 0.672, 0.681]).

links.outcome: discrimination performance variation across patient ethnic subgroups
links.effect: AUROC varied across ethnicities, from 0.704 (95% CI: 0.702, 0.705) for Asian patients to 0.612 (95% CI: 0.609, 0.614) for Black patients.
links.quote: The local model performed best for Asian patients (AUROC = 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705]) and worst for Black patients (AUROC = 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614]).

screen.practice: local validation and model updating (recalibration) before deployment
screen.reason: The study conducts external geographical and temporal validation and demonstrates the impact of model updating/recalibration across regional centers on discrimination, alongside fairness subgroup analysis and health-system reclassification impact analysis.

primary.practice: model updating and recalibration across geographic centers
